content.title: Eid Al-Fitr 2026 Date in US: When Will Eid Be Celebrated? Check Namaz Timings, Prayer Schedule, Moon Sighting Details & How the Eid Date is Decided | All You Need to Know
content.text: Eid al-Fitr 2026 in US: As Ramadan reaches its final stretch, Muslim communities all over America are preparing to observe Eid al-Fitr, a festival that combines elements of religiosity, philanthropy and communalism. As there are 3.5 million Muslims in America, Eid is represented as a wide-ranging, vibrant tapestry that is celebrated in mosques, parks, as well as community centers. The concluding days of Ramadan carry added anticipation, as families wait for confirmation of the festival’s exact date.wait for confirmation of the festival’s exact date. Eid al-Fitr 2026 Date US In 2026, Eid al-Fitr in the United States is expected to fall on Saturday, March 21, though some communities may begin observances on the evening of March 20. The final decision depends on moon sighting reports, which can vary across regions due to geography and local practice. Eid al-Fitr 2026: Check Eid Time in US Moon sighting, often referred to as Chaand Raat is likely on the evening of March 20 and visibility windows differ by city, generally occurring between 6:55 PM and 7:55 PM local time. If the crescent moon is not seen, Ramadan will complete 30 days, placing Eid on March 21. What is Eid al-Fitr? Eid al-Fitr marks the conclusion of Ramadan, a month dedicated to fasting, prayer and reflection where the day begins with a congregational prayer and continues with charity, shared meals and visits among family and friends. In the US, the celebration reflects cultural diversity with traditions varying across communities. Eid al-Fitr 2026: How the Date is Decided The Islamic calendar follows lunar cycles, meaning months begin with the sighting of the crescent moon. In the US, some communities depend on local moon sightings, while others follow global announcements. If the moon is seen on the 29th evening of Ramadan, Eid is the next day otherwise, the fast completes 30 days. Eid al-Fitr 2026: Regional Differences Eid is not celebrated uniformly worldwide while many US communities may align with global announcements, others may observe it based on local sightings. Countries in the Middle East are expected to celebrate on March 20, whereas parts of South Asia may mark Eid on March 21 due to differences in moon visibility.
